sources: Al Jazeera Oct 25 liveblog, 01:20 GMT video entry (live-browser read 05:58-05:59 )
fault_line: Security operation or collective punishment? Hebron's lockdown -- half a million people, a neighbourhood erased -- days before Israel votes.

sections.what_happened: Hebron under lockdown: demolitions left the Farsh al-Hawa area unrecognisable; more than 200 families forced from homes overnight (as recorded at 0500-06); temporary shelters set up; schools told to keep children home two days. This entry adds the named demolished area (Farsh al-Hawa) and the shelter response to the lockdown facts already recorded; it does not add new casualty figures.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA).
sections.what_disputed: No IDF statement or independent verification of the Farsh al-Hawa demolitions was carried in the entry; the lockdown scale (~500,000 people) remains AJ's figure.
sections.why_matters: Hebron's Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhood is now unrecognisable after demolitions -- and the lockdown over nearly half a million Palestinians grinds on, days before Israel's election.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261025-0500-06 (Hebron lockdown) -- AJ Oct 25 liveblog 01:20 GMT video entry: Farsh al-Hawa area left unrecognisable by demolitions; temporary shelters for displaced families

totw_analysis: Our read: Hebron's Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhood is now unrecognisable after demolitions -- and the lockdown over nearly half a million Palestinians grinds on, days before Israel's election. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Security operation or collective punishment? Hebron's lockdown -- half a million people, a neighbourhood erased -- days before Israel votes.
